rewrites.title: Priming and re-stimulation assay with ATAC-seq and AP-1 mapping
rewrites.description: Stimulate cells once, wash out, rest them for several cell cycles, then re-stimulate. Compare the kinetics and magnitude of the second response with naive cells (RNA-seq, nascent RNA), map retained AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding and accessibility at enhancers with ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN, and test whether sites that stay open predict which genes respond faster.

rewrites.title: Sufficiency test with synthetic or optogenetic AP-1 activation and locus-specific editing
rewrites.description: Induce AP-1 with optogenetic or chemically inducible FOS/JUN pulses of varied dose and duration, and use dCas9-based recruitment or CRISPR motif mutation at selected enhancers. Test whether AP-1 binding alone is sufficient to open chromatin and create a stable, restimulation-responsive state, and which sites require it.

rewrites.title: Single-cell live reporters and lineage tracking
rewrites.description: Image AP-1 activity reporters (e.g., a FOS-GFP knock-in or an AP-1 response-element reporter) and track cell lineages through divisions after a pulse. Test whether activity states are inherited by daughter cells more than expected from random sibling pairing, and use single-cell multiome data to link state heritability to chromatin.

rewrites.title: Single-cell lineage tracing of memory inheritance through division
rewrites.description: After transient stimulation, use single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC) with lineage barcodes or sister-cell pairing, plus live imaging of AP-1 reporters or endogenously tagged FOS/JUN. Test whether primed AP-1 target states are inherited by daughter cells and correlate with AP-1 binding retained through mitosis (mitotic bookmarking), compared with unstimulated controls.

rewrites.title: Acute AP-1 perturbation to test necessity and sufficiency
rewrites.description: Remove AP-1 at different times using dominant-negative FOS (A-FOS), degron-tagged JUN/FOS, or CRISPRi/KO, and pulse it with optogenetic or inducible expression. Determine whether AP-1 is needed only to establish the memory or also to maintain it, and whether a pulse alone is sufficient to create it.

rewrites.title: Transient stimulus with longitudinal chromatin accessibility tracking
rewrites.description: Expose cells to a defined transient stimulus (e.g., TPA, TNF, or wounding-like signals), then run ATAC-seq and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) CUT&RUN at multiple time points, including long after the stimulus is gone. Sites that stay open and AP-1 bound after the signal clears, and that respond faster or more strongly on restimulation, would indicate a memory function.

rewrites.title: Transient stimulus with delayed re-challenge and first-pulse AP-1 loss
rewrites.description: Give cells a defined first pulse of a stimulus (e.g., TPA, EGF, or injury cue), rest them for varying intervals, then re-stimulate. Compare transcriptional output (RNA-seq, nascent RNA) with naive cells to test whether AP-1 history changes the second response and how long the change lasts. Include AP-1 loss (dominant-negative FOS/A-Fos, or degron) during the first pulse only, to test whether AP-1 is needed to set the memory.

rewrites.title: Transient stimulus with delayed re-challenge
rewrites.description: Expose cells to a defined AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, TNF, or injury signals), wash it out, then re-stimulate after varying delays (hours to weeks). Measure whether transcriptional output and kinetics of AP-1 targets differ from naive cells, and whether the effect depends on prior AP-1 activity.

rewrites.title: Targeted perturbation of memory-associated sites by CRISPR
rewrites.description: Use dCas9 inhibition or activation, or motif mutagenesis, at persistently accessible AP-1 sites. Test necessity by asking whether editing the AP-1 motif abolishes the primed response at that locus, and sufficiency by asking whether forcing AP-1 binding in naive cells induces a primed state without a stimulus.

rewrites.title: Epigenetic-mechanism coupling and mathematical modeling
rewrites.description: Measure histone modifications, DNA methylation and BAF/SWI-SNF occupancy at AP-1 memory sites, and inhibit these factors (e.g., BRG1 or p300 inhibitors) during the rest period. Fit kinetic models of AP-1 binding, nucleosome remodeling and feedback to the time-course data to test whether AP-1 itself carries memory or depends on a downstream chromatin state.

rewrites.title: Chromatin priming time course after a transient stimulus
rewrites.description: Expose cells to a transient stimulus (e.g., TPA, serum, or injury) and use ATAC-seq and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) CUT&RUN over days to weeks to test whether AP-1-dependent accessible sites persist after the stimulus is gone. Then apply a second challenge to test for faster or stronger transcription at those sites.

rewrites.title: Targeted perturbation of memory-associated AP-1 sites with chromatin conformation readout
rewrites.description: After priming, use CRISPRi/dCas9 epigenome editing or motif mutation at selected AP-1-bound enhancers (identified by persistent accessibility), and combine with Hi-C/Micro-C to look for retained loops. Test whether disrupting the AP-1 site or its recruited BAF/SWI-SNF remodeling erases faster re-induction of linked genes, establishing sufficiency and necessity at specific loci rather than genome-wide correlation.

rewrites.title: Dynamics-encoded memory via optogenetic pulse patterns
rewrites.description: Drive AP-1 with optogenetic or chemogenetic input using varied pulse number, frequency and duration, then measure target gene output and chromatin state after a delay. Fit a model, such as a bistable or hysteresis model, to test whether AP-1 dynamics encode a persistent state that depends on input history.

rewrites.title: Acute degron perturbation at defined memory phases
rewrites.description: Fuse AP-1 subunits (c-JUN, FOSL1, or a dominant-negative like A-FOS) to a degron or place them under inducible control. Remove AP-1 either only during the initial stimulus (testing establishment) or only after the stimulus ends (testing maintenance), then re-challenge the cells. This separates a role for AP-1 in establishing memory from a role in maintaining it, and controls for general cell responsiveness.

rewrites.title: Single-cell paired readout of AP-1 dynamics and re-stimulation response
rewrites.description: Combine live-cell reporters for FOS/JUN activity (or a knock-in fluorescent tag) with a prime–rest–restimulate protocol, followed by single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC). Test whether each cell's AP-1 activity history, such as amplitude and duration, predicts its secondary response, and whether the memory is binary or graded across cells.

rewrites.title: Acute AP-1 degradation at defined times
rewrites.description: Use an inducible degron (e.g., dTAG on c-JUN/FOS) or dominant-negative A-FOS to remove AP-1 either during the priming stimulus or after it has ended. If AP-1 is needed only for establishment, depletion during priming abolishes memory; if it is needed for maintenance, depletion after priming erases it. This separates initiation from maintenance.

rewrites.title: Necessity and sufficiency by acute perturbation
rewrites.description: Use a dominant-negative AP-1 (A-FOS), degron-tagged JUN/FOS, or CRISPRi of specific enhancers, applied either during priming or only during the memory (maintenance) phase, then test whether the memory response is lost. Compare with ectopic AP-1 expression alone to see whether it can create memory without the original signal, to determine whether AP-1 is needed continuously or only to start the memory.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome tracking of memory and heterogeneity
rewrites.description: Perform paired scRNA/scATAC-seq, or live imaging of AP-1 reporters, across stimulation, rest and restimulation. Test whether individual cells with high AP-1 activity retain accessibility and respond more strongly, and whether the state is inherited through cell divisions in lineage-traced clones.

rewrites.title: Acute AP-1 degradation during and after priming
rewrites.description: Use a degron (dTAG/AID) on JUN or FOS, or a dominant-negative such as A-FOS, to deplete AP-1 either only during priming or only after the stimulus has been removed. If AP-1 is needed to establish but not maintain memory, the primed state should persist after depletion in the later window; if it is needed for maintenance, the state should decay. This separates initiation from maintenance.

rewrites.title: Optogenetic or chemogenetic AP-1 induction with sufficiency tests
rewrites.description: Drive JUN/FOS with a light- or drug-inducible system using pulse patterns that differ in duration, frequency, and dimer composition, then remove the input and track target gene expression, chromatin state, and responsiveness to later challenges. Whether a defined pulse pattern is sufficient to create a lasting, heritable state, and whether this depends on dimer identity, would test AP-1 as a causal writer of memory rather than a correlate.
